scenario: 面试官抛出一个建模任务，想看你怎么选模型。你在犹豫要不要直接上 transformer 显得厉害。
scenario_en: The interviewer poses a modeling task to see how you pick a model; you consider reaching straight for a transformer to look impressive.
q: 为什么「模型选择」考的是工程成熟度而不是记忆力？
q_en: Why does model selection test engineering maturity, not recall?
why: 无理由直接上 transformer 会被扣分；先给简单 baseline + 精确的升级判据才是加分项。考的是「取舍推理的流畅度」——按约束选模型、说清代价，而不是背哪个模型最强。
why_en: Reaching for a transformer without justification is penalized; a simple baseline plus precise escalation criteria is rewarded, testing fluency in trade-off reasoning.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  LR["LogReg 基线"] --> GBDT["GBDT 表格"]
  GBDT --> DNN["深度网络 非结构化"]
  DNN --> LLM["LLM 生成/开放域"]
options: 谁能背出最新最强的模型架构，谁就赢
先给简单 baseline + 精确升级判据，考取舍推理流畅度
只要最终精度最高就行，怎么选、为什么这么选、代价多大都不重要
选模型只看训练时间，越快训完越成熟
options_en: Whoever can recite the newest, strongest architecture wins.
A simple baseline plus precise escalation criteria is what earns credit — it tests trade-off fluency.
Only the final accuracy matters; how you chose, why, and what it costs are all irrelevant.
Model choice is judged only by training time — the faster to train, the more mature.
optionExplanations: 背架构是记忆活；面试看的是你能否按约束推理取舍，不是谁记得多。
对；先立 baseline、再给可度量的升级条件，展示的正是工程判断力。
过程和理由恰恰是评分核心——同样精度，能讲清为什么这么选才有信号。
训练时间只是一个成本维度，孤立看它选不出合适模型。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting architectures is rote; interviews look at whether you reason trade-offs under constraints, not who remembers more.
Correct — establishing a baseline then giving measurable escalation conditions shows exactly the engineering judgment being tested.
The process and reasoning are the scoring core — at equal accuracy, explaining why carries the signal.
Training time is one cost axis; judged alone it can't pick the right model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 满足硬约束的最简可行模型，作为对照和升级起点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is the simplest viable model that meets hard constraints, serving as a control and escalation starting point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在明确判据下从简单模型换到更复杂模型（如 GBDT→DNN）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Escalation is moving from a simpler model to a more complex one (e.g. GBDT→DNN) under explicit criteria.

scenario: 你要沿几个固定维度为每个模型选择做辩护。
scenario_en: You must defend every model choice along a fixed set of axes.
q: 模型选择要沿哪五个取舍轴来辩护？(多选)
q_en: Along which five trade-off axes is every model choice defended? (multiple)
why: 五轴：accuracy、latency（服务 SLA）、cost（训练+服务）、interpretability（监管审计）、data requirements（标注门槛）。没有模型能同时最大化五轴。
why_en: Five axes: accuracy, latency, cost, interpretability, and data requirements — and no model maximizes all five at once.
options: accuracy（离线+在线精度）
latency（是否满足服务 SLA）
cost（训练+服务的规模化成本）
interpretability（可解释性，面向监管/利益相关方）
开发者对该框架的个人喜好
options_en: Accuracy (offline + online).
Latency (does it meet the serving SLA?).
Cost (training + serving at scale).
Interpretability (for regulators/stakeholders).
The developer's personal preference for a framework.
optionExplanations: 对；精度是最终效果轴，离线和在线都要看。
对；latency 决定模型能否进线上服务路径。
对；成本覆盖训练与规模化服务，常是排除高端模型的第一刀。
对；可解释性在信贷/医疗等受监管领域是硬约束。
错；个人喜好不是工程取舍轴，漏掉的第五轴是「要多少标注才能赢过替代方案」。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — accuracy is the outcome axis, judged offline and online.
Correct — latency decides whether a model can enter the serving path.
Correct — cost spans training and at-scale serving, often the first cut against high-end models.
Correct — interpretability is a hard constraint in regulated domains like credit/healthcare.
Wrong — personal preference isn't an engineering axis; the missing fifth is how many labels you need to beat the alternative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对延迟/可用性等的服务承诺，如「p99 延迟 <10ms」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service-Level Agreement) is a promised service level such as 'p99 latency < 10ms.'

scenario: 你想找一个「精度最高、延迟最低、成本最低、还最可解释」的完美模型。
scenario_en: You look for one 'best accuracy, lowest latency, lowest cost, most interpretable' perfect model.
q: 为什么不存在在所有轴上都最优的模型？
q_en: Why is there no model optimal on every axis?
why: 因为模型选择在一条 Pareto front（帕累托前沿）上：每次升级都在某轴变好、必在另一轴付代价（如 DNN 精度↑但延迟↑成本↑可解释↓）。所以要按当前约束挑前沿上的一个点，而非追不存在的全能王。
why_en: Model choices lie on a Pareto front where every escalation gains on one axis while paying on another, so you pick a point that fits the constraints.
tradeoff: 沿 Pareto front 取舍（某轴↑另一轴↓） vs 幻想全能模型（不存在）
options: 因为现在工具不够好，等硬件进步后终会出现全能模型
在 Pareto front 上：某轴变好必在另一轴付代价
因为没人愿意花时间调参，调到位就能让所有轴同时最优
因为精度和延迟其实正相关，提升精度会自动把延迟一起降下来
options_en: Because tools are not good enough yet; better hardware will eventually give an all-around model.
On a Pareto front: gaining on one axis always costs you on another.
Because nobody spends the time tuning; tune enough and every axis is optimal at once.
Because accuracy and latency are positively correlated, so raising accuracy also lowers latency.
optionExplanations: 不是硬件问题：取舍是结构性的，DNN 换来精度必付延迟/成本，硬件再好也改不了这个关系。
对；Pareto front 意味着轴与轴此消彼长，只能按约束选前沿上的点。
调参能优化前沿上的位置，但消不掉「一轴换一轴」的本质取舍。
精度和延迟通常负相关（更强模型更慢），说正相关与事实相反。
optionExplanations_en: Not a hardware issue: the trade-off is structural — a DNN's accuracy costs latency/cost regardless of hardware.
Correct — a Pareto front means axes trade off against each other, so you pick a frontier point per constraints.
Tuning improves your position on the frontier but can't erase the essential 'one axis for another' trade-off.
Accuracy and latency are usually negatively correlated (stronger is slower); calling them positive is backwards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组「无法在不牺牲某轴的前提下改进另一轴」的最优取舍点集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Pareto front is the set of optimal trade-off points where no axis can improve without sacrificing another.

scenario: 你要按推理延迟把四大模型族排个序，好知道谁能进严格 SLA 的服务路径。
scenario_en: You rank the four model families by inference latency to know which can enter a strict-SLA serving path.
q: LogReg、GBDT、DNN、LLM 的推理延迟量级大致如何？
q_en: What are the rough inference-latency magnitudes of LogReg, GBDT, DNN, and LLM?
why: 量级：LogReg <1ms、GBDT 1–5ms、DNN 10–100ms（要 GPU）、LLM 100ms–秒级。延迟随精度上限单调上升，这决定了严格 SLA（如 10ms 广告竞价）会先排除 DNN/LLM。
why_en: LogReg <1ms, GBDT 1–5ms, DNN 10–100ms (GPU), LLM 100ms–seconds — latency rises with accuracy ceiling, so strict SLAs rule out DNN/LLM first.
tradeoff: 低延迟（LogReg/GBDT，精度上限低） vs 高延迟（DNN/LLM，精度上限高）
options: 四者推理延迟几乎在同一量级，选模型时不必考虑延迟
LLM <1ms、DNN 1–5ms、GBDT 10–100ms、LogReg 100ms–秒级
LogReg <1ms、GBDT 1–5ms、DNN 10–100ms、LLM 100ms–秒级
只有 GPU 型号影响延迟，模型族本身与推理延迟无关
options_en: All four sit in the same latency magnitude, so latency needn’t factor into the choice.
LLM <1ms, DNN 1–5ms, GBDT 10–100ms, LogReg 100ms–seconds — bigger models are faster.
LogReg <1ms, GBDT 1–5ms, DNN 10–100ms, LLM 100ms–seconds.
Only the GPU model affects latency; the model family itself is unrelated to inference latency.
optionExplanations: 四者延迟差好几个数量级，延迟恰恰是排除模型族的第一刀。
方向反了：越复杂通常越慢，LLM 是最慢的一档。
对；这条延迟阶梯正是「严格 SLA 先淘汰 DNN/LLM」的依据。
模型族的算子复杂度直接决定延迟量级，不是只看 GPU。
optionExplanations_en: The four differ by orders of magnitude; latency is the first cut against families.
Backwards: more complex is usually slower, and LLMs are the slowest tier.
Correct — this latency ladder is why strict SLAs eliminate DNN/LLM first.
A family's operator complexity sets the latency magnitude, not just the GPU.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树（XGBoost/LightGBM），表格数据的高性能低延迟模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees, e.g. XGBoost/LightGBM) is a high-performance, low-latency model for tabular data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度神经网络，对非结构化数据精度上限极高但延迟/成本高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DNN (Deep Neural Network) has a very high accuracy ceiling on unstructured data but higher latency/cost.

scenario: 广告排序系统，要求亚毫秒推理、可解释（监管+调试）、能部署到成千上万个节点。你被问第一步用什么模型。
scenario_en: An ad-ranking system needs sub-ms inference, interpretability (regulatory + debugging), and deploy to thousands of nodes. What's your first model?
q: 广告 CTR 排序的 baseline 该先提什么？
q_en: What baseline should you propose first for ad CTR ranking?
why: 先提逻辑回归：亚毫秒推理满足严格 SLA，特征权重天然可解释，模型只有 KB 级、可轻松铺到上万节点。Meta/Google 的 CTR 长期就靠它——把它作为广告排序 baseline 是正确的第一步。
why_en: Propose logistic regression: sub-ms inference meets the SLA, feature weights are interpretable, and the KB-sized model deploys trivially to thousands of nodes.
tradeoff: LogReg baseline（快/省/可解释，但精度上限低） vs 直接上 DNN（精度高但延迟/成本/黑箱）
options: 先上一个大 transformer 精排模型，精度天花板最高，延迟以后靠工程手段慢慢抠
先提逻辑回归：亚毫秒、权重可解释、模型 KB 级易铺满节点，满足 CTR 的硬约束
先上深度 CNN，广告创意是图片，模型能自动学到视觉特征，不用做特征工程
先上 LLM few-shot 打分，跳过标注和特征工程，反正大模型什么场景都懂
options_en: Start with a big transformer ranker — highest accuracy ceiling; latency can be squeezed out with engineering work later.
Propose logistic regression: sub-ms, interpretable weights, KB-sized to blanket nodes — meeting CTR's hard constraints.
Start with a deep CNN, since ad creatives are images and the model learns visual features on its own — no feature engineering needed.
Start with a few-shot LLM to score, skipping labeling and feature engineering — a big model surely handles any scenario.
whenOtherWins: 当核心信号来自非结构化模态（如广告创意图像/文案语义）、或已有百万级标注且 LogReg 精度触顶时，才升级到 DNN。
whenOtherWins_en: Escalate to a DNN only when the core signal is unstructured (ad creative images/text semantics) or you have millions of labels and LogReg's accuracy has plateaued.
optionExplanations: 大 transformer 精排延迟 100ms–秒，违反亚毫秒 SLA，靠工程手段事后优化也补不回数量级差距。
对；LogReg 一次满足延迟、可解释、易部署三条硬约束，是 CTR 的正确起点。
CTR 排序的核心信号是点击历史等表格特征，创意图片只是其中一个信号源，CNN 学视觉特征替代不了结构化特征工程。
CTR 有海量点击标注，跳过标注去用 LLM few-shot 反而又慢又贵，浪费了已有的丰富标签。
optionExplanations_en: A big transformer ranker runs 100ms–seconds, violating the sub-ms SLA; squeezing it out with engineering later can't recover an order-of-magnitude gap.
Correct — LogReg satisfies latency, interpretability, and deployability at once — the right CTR starting point.
CTR ranking's core signal is tabular features like click history; creative images are just one signal among many, so a CNN's visual features can't replace structured feature engineering.
CTR has abundant click labels; skipping them for a few-shot LLM is slower and costlier, and wastes those labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率，广告/推荐里预测用户点击概率的核心目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the probability a user clicks — a core prediction target in ads/recommendation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性模型经 sigmoid 输出概率，亚毫秒推理、权重可解释。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Logistic regression is a linear model with a sigmoid output; sub-ms inference and interpretable weights.

scenario: 欺诈检测任务：特征是异构表格数据（用户 tenure、设备、价格档、时间），有缺失值，需要建模非线性交互，标注量在几十万级。
scenario_en: Fraud detection: heterogeneous tabular features (tenure, device, price bucket, time) with missing values, needing nonlinear interactions, on hundreds of thousands of labels.
q: 这种表格+缺失值+交互的任务该选什么模型？
q_en: For tabular data with missing values and interactions, which model?
why: 选 GBDT（XGBoost/LightGBM）：自动学非线性与高阶交互、原生处理缺失值（学默认分裂方向）、异构特征无需重预处理、自带特征重要性。表格排序/欺诈正是它的主场，几十万级标注下常胜过 DNN。
why_en: GBDT (XGBoost/LightGBM): it learns nonlinear interactions, natively handles missing values and heterogeneous features, and dominates tabular ranking/fraud at hundreds of thousands of labels.
tradeoff: GBDT（表格/缺失/交互强，标注需求中） vs DNN（非结构化强但表格上易过拟合、需百万级标注）
options: 深度神经网络：它的精度上限最高，任何任务都应该优先考虑它
GBDT（XGBoost）：自动学高阶交互、原生处理缺失值
逻辑回归：线性模型足以，交互和缺失值都不用管
LLM：把表格行拼成文本喂给它做分类
options_en: A deep neural net: it has the highest accuracy ceiling, so it should be preferred for any task.
GBDT (XGBoost): learns high-order interactions and natively handles missing values.
Logistic regression: a linear model suffices; interactions and missing values need no handling.
An LLM: concatenate table rows into text and feed it for classification.
whenOtherWins: 当核心输入变成非结构化（图像/文本/序列），或标注涨到百万级、需要学共享 embedding 表示时，才从 GBDT 升级到 DNN。
whenOtherWins_en: Escalate from GBDT to a DNN when inputs become unstructured (image/text/sequence) or labels reach millions needing shared embedding representations.
optionExplanations: DNN 在几十万级表格上易过拟合、需重调参，精度上限高不代表这里更优，「任何任务优先」是误区。
对；缺失值、异构特征、交互全是 GBDT 的原生强项，几十万标注量正合它。
线性 LogReg 抓不住非线性交互，缺失值也要手工填，欺诈里通常不如 GBDT。
把表格塞进 LLM 又慢又贵，还丢了数值特征的精确性，明显不划算。
optionExplanations_en: A DNN overfits on hundreds of thousands of tabular rows and needs heavy tuning; a high ceiling doesn't make it better here — 'default for any task' is a fallacy.
Correct — missing values, heterogeneous features, and interactions are GBDT's native strengths, matching this label volume.
Linear LogReg can't capture nonlinear interactions and needs manual imputation, usually losing to GBDT on fraud.
Stuffing tables into an LLM is slow, costly, and loses numeric precision — clearly not worth it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 类别型、数值型、序数型混合的特征，GBDT 可原生共存处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Heterogeneous features mix categorical, numeric, and ordinal types, which GBDT handles natively together.

termDefinitions.meaning: GBDT 按分裂增益给出的每个特征贡献度，辅助解释与选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature importance is GBDT's per-feature contribution from split gain, aiding interpretation and selection.

scenario: 你要判断什么时候才有理由从经典模型升级到深度学习。
scenario_en: You must judge when escalating from classical models to deep learning is justified.
q: 哪些信号才构成升级到深度学习的正当理由？(多选)
q_en: Which signals justify escalating to deep learning? (multiple)
why: 三大触发：非结构化输入模态（图像/音频/视频/文本需表示学习）、海量标注（百万级 DNN 才稳胜 GBDT）、复杂交互模式（需稠密 embedding+共享隐空间，如 two-tower 检索）。仅仅「想显得先进」不算理由。
why_en: The triggers are unstructured input modality, massive labeled data (millions), and complex interaction patterns needing dense embeddings — not the wish to look advanced.
options: 输入是非结构化模态（图像/音频/视频/原始文本）
有百万级标注数据，DNN 才稳定超过 GBDT
需要稠密 embedding + 共享隐空间的复杂交互（如 two-tower 检索）
只是想让方案看起来更先进、更唬人
options_en: The input is an unstructured modality (image/audio/video/raw text).
There are millions of labels, where a DNN reliably beats GBDT.
Complex interactions needing dense embeddings + a shared latent space (e.g. two-tower retrieval).
You just want the design to look more advanced and impressive.
optionExplanations: 对；像素/波形的层级特征经典模型学不了，非结构化模态是最硬的升级理由。
对；DNN 只有在百万级标注上才稳胜 GBDT，数据量是关键门槛。
对；检索/排序里的稠密 user/item embedding 与相似度需要深度网络。
错；「显得先进」不是工程理由，无理由升级正是被扣分的行为。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — classical models can't learn hierarchical features from pixels/waveforms, so unstructured modality is the hardest escalation reason.
Correct — a DNN reliably beats GBDT only at millions of labels; data volume is the key threshold.
Correct — dense user/item embeddings and similarity in retrieval/ranking need deep networks.
Wrong — 'looking advanced' isn't an engineering reason; unjustified escalation is exactly what's penalized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从原始输入（像素/波形/文本）自动学出层级特征，是 DNN 相对经典模型的核心优势。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Representation learning automatically learns hierarchical features from raw inputs (pixels/waveforms/text), a DNN's core edge over classical models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔与物品塔各出稠密向量、用相似度检索的架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-tower uses separate user and item towers that emit dense vectors matched by similarity for retrieval.

scenario: Instagram 内容审核：直接对原始图像像素判断是否违规。团队想先用 GBDT 处理。
scenario_en: Instagram content moderation: judge policy violations directly from raw image pixels. The team wants to start with GBDT.
q: 原始图像输入的任务，为什么经典模型不够、要上 DNN？
q_en: For raw-image input, why isn't classical enough and a DNN is needed?
why: 图像是非结构化模态，需要表示学习：CNN/transformer 才能从像素学出层级特征。GBDT/LogReg 吃的是人工表格特征，无法从原始像素学到边缘→纹理→物体这样的层级表示，所以这里必须升级到 DNN。
why_en: Images are unstructured and need representation learning; CNNs/transformers learn hierarchical features from pixels that GBDT can't from hand-crafted tabular inputs.
tradeoff: DNN（能学像素层级特征，但要 GPU/延迟高） vs GBDT（快但吃不了原始像素）
options: GBDT 只要把每个像素当成一列特征就能处理图像，无需升级模型
非结构化像素需表示学习，CNN/DNN 才能学出层级特征
只要把图片压成一个平均颜色值，LogReg 就够了
任何图像任务都只能用 LLM，不能用普通 DNN
options_en: GBDT can handle images by treating each pixel as one feature column — no escalation needed.
Raw pixels are unstructured and need representation learning; only CNNs/DNNs learn hierarchical features.
Just compress each image to one average color and LogReg suffices.
Any image task can only use an LLM, never a plain DNN.
whenOtherWins: 如果图像已被可靠地转成结构化特征（如现成检测器输出的物体计数/属性），下游用 GBDT 反而更快更省。
whenOtherWins_en: If images are already turned into reliable structured features (object counts/attributes from an off-the-shelf detector), a downstream GBDT is faster and cheaper.
optionExplanations: 把像素当独立列丢了空间结构，GBDT 学不到边缘/纹理的层级关系，处理不了原始图像。
对；非结构化模态的层级特征只有深度网络能学，这是最硬的升级理由。
压成平均色丢掉几乎所有信息，审核需要的细节全没了，LogReg 无从判断。
普通 CNN/DNN 完全能做图像审核，不是非 LLM 不可，说法过绝对。
optionExplanations_en: Treating pixels as independent columns loses spatial structure; GBDT can't learn edge/texture hierarchies, so it can't handle raw images.
Correct — only deep networks learn hierarchical features from unstructured modalities — the hardest escalation reason.
Averaging to one color drops nearly all information needed for moderation, leaving LogReg nothing to judge.
Plain CNNs/DNNs handle image moderation fine; it isn't LLM-only — too absolute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 卷积神经网络，擅长从图像像素学空间层级特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) excels at learning spatial hierarchical features from image pixels.

scenario: 表格任务，你在纠结用 GBDT 还是 DNN。手头标注量分别可能是几万、几十万、或几百万。
scenario_en: On a tabular task you weigh GBDT vs DNN; label counts might be tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, or millions.
q: 标注数据量对 GBDT vs DNN 的选择意味着什么？
q_en: What does label volume imply for GBDT vs DNN?
why: 经验门槛：DNN 只有在百万级标注上才稳定超过 GBDT；在此之下（几万~几十万）GBDT 通常更好——更少过拟合、更少调参。这是经验规律不是公式，它决定了「数据不够时不要盲目上 DNN」。
why_en: DNNs reliably beat GBDTs only at millions of labels; below that GBDTs usually win with less overfitting and tuning — an empirical rule, not a formula.
options: 无论标注有多少，DNN 都优于 GBDT，数据量根本不影响选择
DNN 只在百万级标注上才稳胜 GBDT，不足时 GBDT 更好
标注越少越该用 DNN，因为它能靠结构补数据
只有超过十亿标注才该考虑 GBDT，否则一律 DNN
options_en: A DNN beats GBDT no matter the label count; data volume simply doesn’t affect the choice.
A DNN reliably beats GBDT only at millions of labels; below that GBDT wins.
The fewer labels, the more you should use a DNN, since its structure compensates for data.
Only beyond a billion labels should you consider GBDT; otherwise always DNN.
optionExplanations: 数据不足时 DNN 反而过拟合、更难调，说「无论多少都更优」违背经验规律。
对；百万级是 DNN 稳胜的经验门槛，之下 GBDT 在表格上更稳更省。
数据越少 DNN 越容易过拟合，正好相反，不该少数据上 DNN。
门槛反了：数据少反而适合 GBDT，不是十亿以下才用它。
optionExplanations_en: With too little data a DNN overfits and is harder to tune, so 'better regardless' contradicts the rule.
Correct — millions is the empirical threshold where DNN reliably wins; below it GBDT is steadier and cheaper on tabular.
Fewer labels make a DNN overfit more, the opposite — don't use a DNN on little data.
The threshold is reversed: little data favors GBDT, not 'only below a billion.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型记住训练噪声、泛化差；数据不足时 DNN 尤其容易过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overfitting is memorizing training noise and generalizing poorly; DNNs are especially prone to it with insufficient data.

scenario: 你决定从 GBDT 升级到 DNN。面试官追问：升级后线上要付出哪些基础设施代价，你打算怎么接住延迟？
scenario_en: You escalate from GBDT to a DNN. The interviewer probes: what infra costs follow, and how will you meet latency?
q: 升级到 DNN 带来哪些基础设施代价，如何应对延迟？
q_en: What infra costs come with a DNN, and how do you handle latency?
why: 代价：GPU 服务实例（贵）+ INT8/FP16 量化砍 2–4× 延迟 + embedding 缓存。模型选择必须和服务策略成对给出。
why_en: The cost is GPU serving instances plus INT8/FP16 quantization to cut latency two-to-fourfold and embedding caches — model choice must always come paired with a serving strategy.
options: 没有额外代价，DNN 和 GBDT 部署完全一样，用原来的 CPU 集群直接跑
要 GPU 实例、INT8 量化压延迟、embedding 缓存
只要换更快的多核 CPU 撑住 QPS 就行，DNN 推理不需要 GPU
升级后精度自动提高，延迟也会随之下降，不需要额外的量化或缓存改造
options_en: No extra cost; DNN and GBDT deploy identically — just run it on the existing CPU cluster.
You need GPU instances, INT8 quantization to cut latency, and embedding caches.
Just swap to a faster multi-core CPU to hold the QPS; DNN inference doesn't need a GPU.
Escalation raises accuracy and latency drops on its own — no extra quantization or caching rework is needed.
optionExplanations: DNN 需要 GPU 与专门的延迟优化，部署与 GBDT 差别很大，说「原样跑在 CPU 集群上」不成立。
对；GPU+量化+缓存是 DNN 上线的三件套，模型选择必须配套服务策略。
DNN 前向计算是矩阵乘的密集运算，多核 CPU 撑不起 GPU 的并行度，通常还是达不到 SLA。
精度上升不会让延迟自动下降，恰恰相反，没有量化/缓存等服务策略会违反 SLA。
optionExplanations_en: A DNN needs GPUs and dedicated latency work, deploying quite differently from GBDT, so 'run it as-is on the CPU cluster' is false.
Correct — GPU + quantization + caching is the trio for shipping a DNN; model choice must be paired with a serving strategy.
A DNN's forward pass is dense matrix multiplication; a faster multi-core CPU can't match a GPU's parallelism and usually still misses the SLA.
Higher accuracy doesn't lower latency automatically — the opposite — and without quantization/caching the SLA is violated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重/激活从 FP32 降到 INT8/FP16，减小体积、加速推理 2–4 倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers weights/activations from FP32 to INT8/FP16, shrinking the model and speeding inference 2–4x.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计算并缓存稠密向量表示，供线上低延迟取用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding cache precomputes and stores dense vector representations for low-latency online use.

scenario: 候选人在白板上直接画了个大 DNN 说「精度最高选它」，但没提任何在延迟预算内的服务方案。
scenario_en: A candidate sketches a big DNN saying 'highest accuracy, pick it,' with no serving plan within the latency budget.
q: 只选 DNN 却不给服务策略，为什么是常见失误？
q_en: Why is choosing a DNN with no serving strategy a common mistake?
why: 因为 DNN 的 10–100ms 延迟可能直接违反服务 SLA，不配套 GPU/量化/缓存就是纸上谈兵。面试要求「模型选择永远和服务策略成对出现」，只谈精度不谈怎么在预算内上线是典型减分项。
why_en: A DNN's 10–100ms may violate the SLA, so without GPU/quantization/caching it's unshippable; model choice must always pair with a serving strategy.
tradeoff: 模型选择+服务策略成对（可落地） vs 只谈精度（漂亮但上不了线）
options: 不是失误，精度最高的模型就该选，上线部署和延迟细节交给基础设施团队去操心
DNN 的 10–100ms 可能违反 SLA，选择必须配套服务策略
失误在于 DNN 训练成本太便宜，该选参数量更大的模型显示团队技术实力
只要模型精度够高，10–100ms 的延迟用户感知不到，不必额外优化
options_en: Not a mistake — pick the most accurate model and leave deployment and latency details to the infra team.
A DNN’s 10–100ms may violate the SLA, so the choice must come with a serving strategy.
The mistake is that a DNN is too cheap to train; pick a model with more parameters to show the team's technical chops.
As long as accuracy is high enough, users won't perceive a 10–100ms delay, so no extra work is needed.
optionExplanations: 上线可行性是模型选择的一部分，甩给基础设施团队恰恰是面试要避免的脱节。
对；不谈如何在延迟预算内服务，DNN 的高精度就是空中楼阁，这正是失分点。
训练成本低不是缺点、参数量大也不代表更适合场景；选贵模型显实力是错误取舍观。
线上有硬 SLA，即使用户感知不到 10–100ms，请求超预算也会被网关按 SLA 丢弃或超时。
optionExplanations_en: Deployability is part of model choice; offloading it to infra is exactly the disconnect interviews penalize.
Correct — without serving within the latency budget, the DNN's accuracy is castles in the air — the losing point.
Low training cost isn't a flaw and more parameters don't mean better fit; picking a pricier model 'for street cred' is a wrong trade-off mindset.
Online has a hard SLA; even if users don't perceive 10–100ms, over-budget requests are still dropped or time out at the gateway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让选定模型在延迟/成本预算内上线的方案（GPU、量化、缓存、批处理等）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A serving strategy is the plan to ship the chosen model within latency/cost budgets (GPU, quantization, caching, batching).

scenario: 实时竞价（RTB）：10ms 延迟 SLA，输入是 50 个人工工程化的表格特征，标注充足。
scenario_en: Real-time bidding (RTB): a 10ms latency SLA, 50 engineered tabular features, ample labels.
q: 这个 10ms/表格特征的场景该选什么模型栈？
q_en: For this 10ms/tabular scenario, which model stack?
why: 选 GBDT（LightGBM）跑这 50 个表格特征，逻辑回归做初始 baseline。表格+严格延迟正好排除 DNN/LLM，GBDT 精度好且 1–5ms 卡进 10ms SLA，LogReg 作对照起步。
why_en: GBDT (LightGBM) on the 50 tabular features with logistic regression as the initial baseline; tabular + strict latency rules out DNN/LLM.
tradeoff: GBDT/LogReg（1–5ms 卡进 SLA，表格强） vs DNN/LLM（精度上限高但延迟超 10ms）
options: 深度神经网络：精度上限最高，值得为它把 10ms SLA 放宽到几十毫秒
GBDT（LightGBM）跑 50 个表格特征，逻辑回归做初始 baseline
LLM few-shot：省得为 50 个特征做特征工程，标注数据也用不上
多模态 transformer：把 50 个表格特征当 token 序列，学交叉特征
options_en: A deep neural net: highest accuracy ceiling, worth relaxing the 10ms SLA to tens of ms for.
GBDT (LightGBM) on the 50 tabular features, with logistic regression as the initial baseline.
A few-shot LLM: skip feature engineering on the 50 features, and skip the labeled data too.
A multimodal transformer: feed the 50 tabular features as a token sequence to learn crosses.
whenOtherWins: 如果延迟预算放宽到几十 ms、且核心信号来自非结构化模态或需要学习交叉特征，才考虑升级到 DNN。
whenOtherWins_en: Only if the latency budget loosens to tens of ms and the core signal is unstructured or needs learned crosses would you escalate to a DNN.
optionExplanations: SLA 是硬约束不能为模型放宽；DNN 10–100ms 直接违反 10ms 竞价预算。
对；表格+10ms 的组合正是 GBDT 主场，LogReg 打底、LightGBM 承接精度。
标注充足时跳过标注去用 LLM few-shot 又慢又贵，还违反 10ms SLA，白白浪费已有标签。
50 个表格特征本就适合树模型直接切分，不需要 transformer 的序列建模学交叉，量级和延迟都不划算。
optionExplanations_en: The SLA is a hard constraint, not to be relaxed for a model; a DNN's 10–100ms violates the 10ms bidding budget.
Correct — tabular + 10ms is GBDT's home turf, with LogReg as baseline and LightGBM carrying accuracy.
With ample labels, skipping them for a few-shot LLM is slow, costly, and breaks the 10ms SLA, wasting the labels for nothing.
50 tabular features are already well split by tree models — they don't need a transformer's sequence modeling to learn crosses, and it's wrong on both scale and latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: leaf-wise 生长的 GBDT 实现，大数据上训练快，适合表格排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LightGBM is a leaf-wise GBDT implementation, fast to train on large data, suited to tabular ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时广告竞价，通常有个位数到十几毫秒的严格延迟预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTB (Real-Time Bidding) is real-time ad auctioning with a strict single-to-low-double-digit-ms latency budget.

scenario: 你要判断一个任务是否真的适合用 LLM，而不是任务专用模型。
scenario_en: You judge whether a task genuinely suits an LLM rather than a task-specific model.
q: 什么情况下用 LLM 才是对的选择？(多选)
q_en: When is an LLM the right choice? (multiple)
why: LLM 适合：需要生成式输出（摘要/对话）、开放式输出空间（无法枚举）、标注稀缺（few/zero-shot 冷启动）、需要广博世界知识（开放域 QA）。分类/排序且标注充足时它反而不是好选择。
why_en: Use an LLM for generative output, open-ended output spaces, scarce labels (few/zero-shot cold start), and broad world knowledge — not for well-labeled classification/ranking.
options: 需要生成式输出（摘要、对话）
输出空间开放、无法枚举所有可能答案
标注数据稀缺，靠 few-/zero-shot 冷启动
有百万级标注的定义明确的二分类任务
options_en: Generative output is required (summarization, dialogue).
The output space is open-ended and can't be enumerated.
Labels are scarce, relying on few-/zero-shot cold start.
A well-defined binary classification task with millions of labels.
optionExplanations: 对；生成自然语言正是 LLM 的核心能力，专用分类器做不了。
对；输出无法枚举时，LLM 的开放生成能力不可替代。
对；标注稀缺/冷启动时 few-shot LLM 能不训就用，最省。
错；标注充足的明确分类该用 GBDT——更快更便宜更准，LLM 反而是错配。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — generating natural language is the LLM's core ability that a task classifier lacks.
Correct — when outputs can't be enumerated, the LLM's open-ended generation is irreplaceable.
Correct — with scarce labels/cold start, a few-shot LLM works without training — cheapest.
Wrong — well-labeled, well-defined classification should use GBDT (faster, cheaper, more accurate); an LLM is a mismatch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，擅长生成、开放域与 few-/zero-shot，但延迟/成本高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LLM (Large Language Model) excels at generation, open-domain tasks, and few-/zero-shot, but at high latency/cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不训练（zero）或仅给几个示例（few）就让模型完成新任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-shot means no training and few-shot means a handful of examples to perform a new task.

scenario: 面试官想听你在什么情况下会主动说「这里不该用 LLM」，并给出取舍理由。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants to hear when you'd proactively say 'an LLM is wrong here,' with trade-off reasons.
q: 哪些情况下 LLM 是错误选择？(多选)
q_en: In which cases is an LLM the wrong choice? (multiple)
why: LLM 不宜：标注充足的明确分类（GBDT 更快更准）、毫秒 SLA、十亿级请求成本、监管要可审计归因。它的强项是开放域生成。
why_en: An LLM is the wrong pick for well-labeled classification, millisecond SLAs, billion-request cost pressure, or audit-grade attribution — its strength is open-domain generation.
options: 定义明确、标注充足的分类/排序（如百万级欺诈）
严格延迟 SLA（广告竞价、ETA 等毫秒级）
十亿级请求规模、成本极度敏感
需要开放域世界知识的自由问答
options_en: Well-defined, well-labeled classification/ranking (e.g. million-scale fraud).
Strict latency SLAs (ad bidding, ETA, at millisecond scale).
Billions of requests with extreme cost sensitivity.
Open-domain free-form QA needing broad world knowledge.
optionExplanations: 对；标注充足的明确分类 GBDT 更快更准更省，LLM 是错配。
对；LLM 100ms–秒级延迟违反毫秒 SLA，竞价/ETA 用不了。
对；十亿级请求下 LLM 成本天文，LR 便宜几个数量级。
错；开放域自由问答恰恰是 LLM 的强项，这里该用它，不是错误选择。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — for well-labeled classification, GBDT is faster, more accurate, and cheaper; an LLM is a mismatch.
Correct — an LLM's 100ms–seconds violates millisecond SLAs, unusable for bidding/ETA.
Correct — at billions of requests an LLM's cost is astronomical; LR is orders cheaper.
Wrong — open-domain free-form QA is exactly the LLM's strength — the right choice, not wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每次预测按特征分配贡献的可解释方法，常配 GBDT 满足监管审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attributes each prediction to features, often paired with GBDT to satisfy regulatory audit.

tradeoff: LLM 的通用/生成能力 vs 专用模型的低延迟、低成本与可审计性

scenario: Uber 要预测 ETA（预计到达时间），输入是距离、路况、时段等结构化特征，需毫秒级、可解释、海量请求。
scenario_en: Uber predicts ETA from structured features (distance, traffic, time of day), needing millisecond, interpretable, high-volume inference.
q: Uber ETA 预测该选什么模型，为什么不是 LLM？
q_en: Which model for Uber ETA, and why not an LLM?
why: 选 GBDT 跑距离/路况/时段这些结构化特征：毫秒级、精度好、可解释、海量请求成本低。ETA 是定义明确的表格回归，用 LLM 又慢又贵还不准——「说 LLM 不合适并给出取舍」比默认上大模型更有信号。
why_en: GBDT on structured distance/traffic/time features: millisecond, accurate, interpretable, cheap at scale; ETA is well-defined tabular regression where an LLM is absurd.
tradeoff: GBDT（毫秒/可解释/便宜，表格回归） vs LLM（慢、贵、对表格回归不准）
options: LLM：让它读路况描述文本推理出到达时间
GBDT：跑距离/路况/时段等结构化特征，毫秒级、可解释、海量请求便宜
大 transformer：把 ETA 当成序列生成任务来做，更前沿
纯逻辑回归：ETA 一定是完美线性的，无需非线性模型
options_en: An LLM: have it read traffic descriptions and reason out the arrival time.
GBDT: on structured distance/traffic/time features — millisecond, interpretable, cheap at high volume.
A big transformer: treat ETA as a sequence-generation task — more cutting-edge.
Plain logistic regression: ETA is surely perfectly linear, no nonlinear model needed.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务变成「根据用户自由文本行程需求生成解释性回复」，那才轮到 LLM；纯数值 ETA 回归不需要它。
whenOtherWins_en: If the task became 'generate an explanatory reply to a user's free-text trip request,' an LLM fits; pure numeric ETA regression doesn't need one.
optionExplanations: 把结构化数值任务硬塞给 LLM 又慢又贵、精度还差，是典型错配。
对；ETA 是表格回归，GBDT 满足毫秒/可解释/低成本，是标准答案。
序列生成 transformer 对数值回归属杀鸡用牛刀，延迟成本都不划算。
LogReg 是分类模型且假设线性，ETA 有明显非线性交互（路况×时段），欠拟合。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing a structured numeric task onto an LLM is slow, costly, and less accurate — a classic mismatch.
Correct — ETA is tabular regression; GBDT meets millisecond/interpretable/low-cost — the standard answer.
A sequence-generation transformer for numeric regression is overkill, poor on both latency and cost.
LogReg is a classifier assuming linearity; ETA has clear nonlinear interactions (traffic × time), so it underfits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间，一个基于结构化特征的数值回归任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) is a numeric regression task from structured features.

scenario: 客服机器人要在几十个类别上理解用户自由文本并生成自然语言回复，很多长尾问法没有充足标注。
scenario_en: A support chatbot must understand free-text over dozens of categories and generate natural-language replies, with many long-tail phrasings poorly labeled.
q: 这种自由文本、生成式、标注稀疏的客服场景该选什么？
q_en: For free-text, generative, sparsely-labeled support, which model?
why: 选 LLM：要生成自然语言回复（生成式输出）、覆盖几十类且长尾问法多（开放式）、标注稀疏可靠 few-shot 冷启动。这几条正好命中 LLM 的适用面，专用分类器覆盖不了长尾也不会生成。
why_en: An LLM: it generates natural-language replies, covers open-ended long-tail phrasings across dozens of categories, and cold-starts with few-shot on sparse labels.
tradeoff: LLM（生成+开放+few-shot，但慢/贵） vs 专用分类器（快但不会生成、覆盖不了长尾）
options: GBDT：把用户文本 one-hot 成几万列表格特征后做多分类
LLM：生成自然语言回复、覆盖开放长尾、few-shot 冷启动
逻辑回归：几十个类别用线性多分类足够
只做关键词规则匹配，不用任何模型
options_en: GBDT: one-hot the user text into tens of thousands of feature columns, then do multiclass.
LLM: it generates natural-language replies, covers the open-ended long tail, and few-shot cold-starts.
Logistic regression: linear multiclass suffices for dozens of categories.
Keyword rule matching only, with no model.
whenOtherWins: 如果类别固定、封闭、且每类都有充足标注、只需分类不需生成回复，那专用分类器（GBDT/微调小模型）更快更省。
whenOtherWins_en: If categories are fixed and closed with ample labels and you only classify (no generated reply), a task-specific classifier (GBDT/fine-tuned small model) is faster and cheaper.
optionExplanations: one-hot 文本丢语义、覆盖不了长尾问法，且 GBDT 不会生成自然语言回复。
对；生成+开放+few-shot 三条都命中 LLM，正是它的主场。
线性多分类抓不住自由文本语义，也不生成回复，长尾问法直接漏掉。
纯规则脆弱、无法泛化到新问法，覆盖几十类长尾会大量漏判。
optionExplanations_en: One-hot text loses semantics and misses long-tail phrasings, and GBDT can't generate natural-language replies.
Correct — generative + open-ended + few-shot all point to the LLM — its home turf.
Linear multiclass can't capture free-text semantics or generate replies, dropping long-tail phrasings.
Pure rules are brittle and don't generalize to new phrasings, missing much of the long tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出现频率低但种类繁多的问法/样本，规则和小分类器难覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The long tail is low-frequency but highly varied cases/phrasings that rules and small classifiers struggle to cover.

scenario: 面试的模型选择环节，你要在 45 分钟里花 5–7 分钟走一套可复现的选型流程。
scenario_en: In the model-selection segment you spend 5–7 minutes of a 45-minute interview on a repeatable selection protocol.
q: 把模型选择的 5 步协议排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 5-step model-selection protocol:
steps: 澄清任务与模态：分类/排序/检索/生成？表格/文本/图像/多模态？
识别硬约束：延迟 SLA、可解释性、数据量、服务预算（先于精度淘汰模型族）
提出最简可行 baseline：满足硬约束的最低复杂度方案，并明说出来
给出可度量的升级判据：如「离线 AUC<0.75 就升级到带 embedding 的 DNN」
讨论运营影响：GPU 服务、量化、drift 监控、A/B 测试精度-延迟取舍
why: 顺序是先澄清任务模态→用硬约束淘汰模型族（在谈精度之前）→提最简 baseline→给可度量升级判据→谈运营。关键：硬约束（延迟/可解释/数据/预算）要在比精度之前就把不合规的族淘汰掉。
why_en: Clarify task/modality, then let hard constraints eliminate families before accuracy, propose the simplest baseline, give measurable escalation criteria, then discuss operations.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["1 澄清任务/模态"] --> B["2 硬约束淘汰模型族"]
  B --> C["3 最简 baseline"]
  C --> D["4 可度量升级判据"]
  D --> E["5 运营影响"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟 SLA、可解释性、数据量、服务预算等在比精度之前就淘汰模型族的要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard constraints (latency SLA, interpretability, data volume, serving budget) eliminate model families before accuracy is even discussed.

scenario: 一个任务同时有 5ms 延迟 SLA 和信贷监管的可解释要求，也有人主张「先比各模型精度再说」。
scenario_en: A task has both a 5ms latency SLA and credit-regulation interpretability needs; someone argues 'compare accuracies first.'
q: 选型时硬约束和精度谁先谁后？
q_en: In selection, do hard constraints or accuracy come first?
why: 硬约束先行：延迟 SLA、可解释性、数据量、服务预算要在比精度之前就把不合规的模型族淘汰掉。一个违反 5ms 或无法解释的模型，精度再高也出局——先过约束的筛子，再在剩下的里比精度。
why_en: Hard constraints come first: latency, interpretability, data, and budget eliminate non-compliant families before accuracy is compared.
tradeoff: 先淘汰不合约束的族再比精度（高效） vs 先比精度（可能选中一个根本上不了线的模型）
options: 先比精度，谁最高就选谁，之后再想办法满足延迟和监管约束
硬约束先行：延迟/可解释/数据/预算先淘汰不合规的族
两者无所谓先后，凭直觉同时权衡即可
只看可解释性，其它约束都不重要
options_en: Compare accuracy first, pick the highest, then find ways to meet latency and regulatory constraints.
Hard constraints first: latency, interpretability, data and budget rule out families.
Order doesn't matter; weigh everything at once by intuition.
Only interpretability matters; other constraints are unimportant.
whenOtherWins: 只有当所有候选模型都已满足硬约束时，精度才成为区分它们的主维度。
whenOtherWins_en: Only once all candidates already satisfy the hard constraints does accuracy become the main differentiator.
optionExplanations: 先比精度可能选中违反 5ms 或不可解释的模型，「之后满足约束」往往根本做不到。
对；约束是筛子，先淘汰上不了线的族，能省下大量无效比较。
无先后会让不合规模型混入候选，浪费时间在注定出局的选项上。
只看可解释性会漏掉 5ms 延迟这条同样致命的硬约束，覆盖不全。
optionExplanations_en: Accuracy-first may pick a model that violates 5ms or isn't interpretable, and 'satisfy constraints later' often can't be done.
Correct — constraints are a sieve; eliminating unshippable families first saves much wasted comparison.
No ordering lets non-compliant models into the pool, wasting time on doomed options.
Interpretability-only misses the equally fatal 5ms latency constraint — incomplete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用硬约束剔除不合规模型族，再在合规者中按精度等排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eliminate-then-rank first removes non-compliant families via hard constraints, then ranks survivors by accuracy.

scenario: 面试官问：你说会「必要时升级到深度学习」，那具体什么触发升级？他想听可度量的判据。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: you said you'd 'escalate to deep learning if needed' — what triggers it, measurably?
q: 升级判据该怎么表述才够专业？
q_en: How should an escalation criterion be phrased to sound senior?
why: 用可度量的阈值，如「若离线 AUC<0.75 就升级到带 embedding 特征的 DNN」。含糊的「不够好就升级」不可执行；给出具体指标+阈值+目标模型，才展示你有明确的实验止损与升级计划。
why_en: Use a measurable threshold like 'if offline AUC < 0.75, escalate to a DNN with embedding features,' not a vague 'escalate if not good enough.'
tradeoff: 可度量判据（可执行、有止损） vs 含糊判据（无法触发、显得没计划）
options: 「如果上线之后效果不太理想，就换一个更强更大的模型，慢慢试到满意为止」
「离线 AUC<0.75 就升级到 embedding 特征 DNN」
「先把逻辑回归、GBDT、DNN 都训一遍，哪个顺眼就用哪个」
「先不设阈值，等上线出问题了、用户投诉了再回头考虑升级」
options_en: “If it doesn’t look great after launch, we’ll swap in a bigger, stronger model and keep trying until it feels right.”
“If offline AUC drops below 0.75, escalate to a DNN with embedding features.”
'Train logistic regression, GBDT, and a DNN, and use whichever feels right.'
'Skip setting a threshold; wait until production breaks and users complain, then reconsider escalating.'
whenOtherWins: 在探索早期、指标体系还没定好时，可以先做定性摸底；但一旦要写选型计划，就必须给可度量阈值。
whenOtherWins_en: In very early exploration before metrics are defined, a qualitative probe is fine; but any written selection plan needs a measurable threshold.
optionExplanations: 「效果不好」无法度量、无法触发，反复换模型也不知道何时该停，等于没有升级计划。
对；指标+阈值+目标模型三件齐全，才是可执行、可复现的升级判据。
「哪个顺眼」是训完再拍脑袋，不是可以提前写进计划、向他人复现的工程判据。
不设阈值、等出问题再升级是被动救火，面试要的是前置的可度量止损线。
optionExplanations_en: 'Doesn't work great' is unmeasurable and untriggerable; repeatedly swapping models with no stopping rule is effectively no escalation plan.
Correct — metric + threshold + target model together make an executable, reproducible escalation criterion.
'Whichever feels right' is a post-hoc gut call after training everything, not an engineering criterion you can write into a plan up front.
Setting no threshold and escalating only after breakage is reactive firefighting; interviews want a proactive measurable stop-loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分类排序能力的指标，常作升级阈值（如 <0.75 升级）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures ranking ability and often serves as an escalation threshold (e.g. < 0.75 escalate).

scenario: 信贷/医疗等受监管领域要求对每个预测给出可审计的解释。你要对比各模型的可解释性。
scenario_en: Regulated domains (credit/health) require auditable per-prediction explanations; you compare model interpretability.
q: 四大模型族在可解释性上如何排序？
q_en: How do the four families rank on interpretability?
why: LogReg 最可解释（直接看特征权重）；GBDT 中等（靠 SHAP 做逐预测归因）；DNN 低（黑箱，需 SHAP/LIME 事后近似）；LLM 最低（推理链不可审计）。监管场景优先 LogReg/GBDT+SHAP。
why_en: LogReg is most interpretable (feature weights), GBDT moderate (SHAP), DNN low (black box needing SHAP/LIME), LLM lowest — regulated domains prefer LogReg/GBDT+SHAP.
tradeoff: 可解释（LogReg/GBDT+SHAP，满足监管） vs 黑箱（DNN/LLM，精度高但难审计）
options: LLM 最可解释，因为它能用自然语言把自己的推理过程讲出来给审计看
LogReg（权重）> GBDT（SHAP）> DNN > LLM
四者可解释性其实相同，都能满足监管的逐笔审计要求
DNN 最可解释，因为它层数多、每层结构都很清晰
options_en: The LLM is most interpretable because it can narrate its own reasoning in natural language for auditors.
LogReg (weights) > GBDT (SHAP) > DNN > LLM.
All four are equally interpretable and all satisfy per-decision regulatory audit.
The DNN is most interpretable because it has many layers, each with clear structure.
optionExplanations: LLM 的自然语言「解释」不是可审计的因果归因，监管不认，最可解释说反了。
对；SHAP 让 GBDT 能给每一笔预测做逐特征归因，这是它进得了信贷风控而 DNN 进不了的关键差。
四者可解释性差距巨大，说相同会让你在信贷/医疗里选错模型。
层数多恰恰更黑箱，DNN 可解释性低，不是高。
optionExplanations_en: An LLM's natural-language 'explanation' isn't auditable causal attribution and regulators don't accept it — most-interpretable is backwards.
Correct — SHAP lets GBDT attribute every single prediction feature by feature, the exact gap that gets it into credit risk where a DNN can’t go.
The four differ vastly; calling them equal leads to the wrong model in credit/health.
More layers means more of a black box; DNN interpretability is low, not high.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用局部线性代理解释单个预测的事后可解释方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) explains a single prediction via a local linear surrogate, post hoc.

scenario: 信用评分模型：监管（ECOA/GDPR）要求对每个拒贷决定给出可审计的逐特征解释。团队有人想用 LLM 提精度。
scenario_en: A credit-scoring model must give auditable per-feature explanations for each denial (ECOA/GDPR); someone wants an LLM for accuracy.
q: 受监管的信用评分该选什么，为什么不是 LLM/DNN？
q_en: For regulated credit scoring, which model, and why not LLM/DNN?
why: 选 GBDT + SHAP：既有强表格精度，又能对每个决定给逐特征归因，满足 ECOA/GDPR 审计。LLM/DNN 是黑箱，其推理无法作为拒贷的合规解释——监管可解释性是硬约束，直接排除它们。
why_en: GBDT + SHAP: strong tabular accuracy plus per-feature attribution for each decision, satisfying ECOA/GDPR, whereas LLM/DNN reasoning isn't auditable.
tradeoff: GBDT+SHAP（可审计+表格精度） vs LLM/DNN（精度高但黑箱、不满足监管）
options: LLM：让它用自然语言给每一笔拒贷都写一段解释，就能满足监管审计
GBDT + SHAP：强表格精度 + 逐特征可审计归因
深度神经网络：精度最高，可解释性用不着管
随机猜测模型：反正解释不重要
options_en: An LLM: have it write a natural-language explanation for every denial to satisfy the audit.
GBDT + SHAP: strong tabular accuracy plus auditable per-feature attribution.
A deep neural net: highest accuracy; interpretability doesn't matter.
A random-guess model, since explanations don't matter.
whenOtherWins: 如果该场景不受监管、不需要逐决定解释，且核心信号来自非结构化数据，才可能考虑 DNN 换取更高精度。
whenOtherWins_en: Only in an unregulated case with no per-decision explanation need and unstructured core signal would you consider a DNN for higher accuracy.
optionExplanations: LLM 的自然语言解释不是可审计的因果归因，监管不认，满足不了 ECOA/GDPR。
对；GBDT 精度好、SHAP 给逐特征归因，正好卡住监管可解释这条硬约束。
受监管场景可解释是硬约束，DNN 黑箱直接出局，「用不着管」是错的。
随机模型既不准也不可解释，是明显的荒谬项。
optionExplanations_en: An LLM's natural-language explanation isn't auditable causal attribution; regulators reject it, failing ECOA/GDPR.
Correct — GBDT is accurate and SHAP gives per-feature attribution, meeting the regulatory-interpretability constraint.
In regulated domains interpretability is a hard constraint, so the black-box DNN is out — 'doesn't matter' is wrong.
A random model is neither accurate nor interpretable — an obviously absurd option.

termDefinitions.meaning: 美国信贷公平法，要求对信贷决定给出具体、可审计的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ECOA (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) is a US fair-lending law requiring specific, auditable reasons for credit decisions.

scenario: 一个功能每天要跑数十亿次推理，单位成本会被放大数十亿倍，团队对推理成本极度敏感。
scenario_en: A feature runs billions of inferences daily, amplifying unit cost billions-fold; the team is extremely cost-sensitive.
q: 十亿级请求、成本极敏感时，模型选择偏向什么？
q_en: At billions of requests with tight cost, which way does model choice lean?
why: 偏向最便宜的可行模型，如逻辑回归——单次推理只是点积+sigmoid，在 CPU 上比 LLM 便宜几个数量级。十亿级规模下，单位成本差被乘以十亿，成本从「次要」升为「首要」约束。
why_en: Lean to the cheapest viable model like logistic regression — a dot product on CPU is orders of magnitude cheaper than an LLM, and at billions of requests unit cost dominates.
tradeoff: LR（每次点积、CPU、极便宜） vs LLM（每次 GPU/API 调用、成本×十亿爆炸）
options: 偏向 LLM，反正请求规模越大，越能摊薄单位推理成本
偏向最便宜的可行模型，如 LR（CPU 上一次点积）
成本与请求量无关，选模型只看精度
请求越多越该上最贵的模型，显得系统重要
options_en: Lean to an LLM; the larger the request volume, the better the unit inference cost amortizes.
Lean to the cheapest viable model, e.g. LR — one CPU dot product per request.
Cost is unrelated to request volume; choose by accuracy only.
The more requests, the pricier the model should be, to signal importance.
optionExplanations: 规模大不会摊薄 LLM 的单次成本，反而把每次的高成本乘以十亿，越用越贵。
对；LR 的点积推理在 CPU 上便宜几个数量级，十亿级规模下成本成了硬约束。
成本恰恰随请求量线性放大，忽略它会在规模上算崩预算。
请求多更该压单位成本，不是选更贵模型，逻辑反了。
optionExplanations_en: Scale doesn't amortize an LLM's per-call cost; it multiplies the high per-call cost by billions — pricier the more you use it.
Correct — LR's dot-product inference on CPU is orders cheaper, and at billions of requests cost becomes a hard constraint.
Cost scales linearly with volume; ignoring it blows the budget at scale.
More requests means driving unit cost down, not picking a pricier model — reversed logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单次推理的成本，在十亿级请求下被放大成主导预算的因素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Unit cost is the cost per inference, amplified into a budget-dominating factor at billions of requests.

q: 补全模型选择的五个取舍轴：
q_en: Fill in the five model-selection trade-off axes.
text: 五轴：{{accuracy}}（精度）、{{latency}}（延迟/SLA）、{{cost}}（训练+服务成本）、{{interpretability}}（可解释性）、data {{requirements}}（数据需求）。没有模型能在五轴同时最优。
text_en: The five axes: {{accuracy}}, {{latency}} (SLA), {{cost}} (train+serve), {{interpretability}}, and data {{requirements}} — no model is optimal on all five.
why: 记忆钩子：精度、延迟、成本、可解释、数据需求。每次升级在其中一轴变好、另一轴付代价。
why_en: Memory hook: accuracy, latency, cost, interpretability, data — each escalation gains on one axis and pays on another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达到某模型有效性所需的标注量，是选型的第五轴。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data requirements are the labeled-data volume needed for a model to be effective — the fifth selection axis.

scenario: 面试官想区分候选人是「只会挑模型」还是「会设计选型策略」。
scenario_en: The interviewer distinguishes candidates who 'just pick models' from those who 'design a selection strategy.'
q: 初级和资深工程师在模型选择上的差别是什么？
q_en: What separates junior and senior engineers in model selection?
why: 初级工程师「挑模型」；资深工程师设计贯穿训练→服务→监控的选型策略——先给 baseline、定可度量升级判据、配服务与漂移监控。展示的是端到端策略，不是一个孤立的模型名。
why_en: Juniors pick a model; seniors design a selection strategy spanning training, serving, and monitoring — baseline, escalation criteria, serving, and drift.
options: 资深工程师总是选最复杂的模型，初级工程师只敢选简单的
初级挑一个模型；资深设计训练→服务→监控的选型策略
两者没区别，选型全凭经验直觉
资深工程师从不写 baseline，直接上最终模型
options_en: Seniors always pick the most complex model while juniors only dare pick simple ones.
Juniors pick a model; seniors design a selection strategy spanning training, serving and monitoring.
No difference; selection is all intuition.
Seniors never write a baseline and go straight to the final model.
optionExplanations: 资深恰恰倾向从简单 baseline 起步，不是无脑选最复杂，说反了。
对；差别在于「策略 vs 单点」——端到端设计选型流程才是资深信号。
选型有可复现的方法论，不是纯直觉，说没区别抹掉了核心评分点。
资深工程师正是强调先立 baseline，跳过 baseline 是初级常见错误。
optionExplanations_en: Seniors tend to start from a simple baseline, not blindly pick the most complex — reversed.
Correct — the difference is 'strategy vs single pick'; designing an end-to-end selection process is the senior signal.
Selection has a reproducible methodology, not pure intuition; 'no difference' erases the core scoring point.
Seniors emphasize establishing a baseline first; skipping it is a common junior mistake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 覆盖 baseline、升级判据、服务与监控的端到端模型选择方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A selection strategy is the end-to-end plan covering baseline, escalation criteria, serving, and monitoring.

scenario: 有人想在 10ms SLA 的广告竞价里用 LLM 打分，理由是「LLM 更聪明」。
scenario_en: Someone wants an LLM scoring in a 10ms-SLA ad auction because 'LLMs are smarter.'
q: 为什么 LLM 进不了毫秒级 SLA 的服务路径？
q_en: Why can't an LLM enter a millisecond-SLA serving path?
why: LLM 推理延迟在 100ms–秒级，比 10ms 预算高一到两个数量级，直接违反竞价/ETA 的硬 SLA。这不是调优能补的差距，延迟量级本身就把 LLM 排除在毫秒级服务之外。
why_en: An LLM's 100ms–seconds latency is one to two orders above a 10ms budget, hard-violating the SLA — a gap tuning can't close.
tradeoff: 毫秒级模型（LR/GBDT，卡进 SLA） vs LLM（100ms–秒，量级超标）
options: 能进，只要多加几台 GPU 并行推理，就能把 LLM 压到 10ms 以内
LLM 的 100ms–秒比 10ms 预算高一两个数量级，调优补不回
能进，LLM 其实是所有模型里最快的
SLA 只是建议值，超一点没关系，LLM 照样能用
options_en: It can — just add a few GPUs for parallel inference to squeeze the LLM under 10ms.
An LLM’s 100ms–seconds is one to two orders above a 10ms budget; tuning can’t close that gap.
It can; an LLM is actually the fastest of all models.
The SLA is just advisory; a slight overshoot is fine and the LLM still works.
optionExplanations: 加 GPU 提高吞吐但压不掉单次生成的固有延迟，量级差堆机器补不回。
对；100ms–秒 vs 10ms 是数量级差，硬 SLA 面前 LLM 直接出局。
LLM 是最慢的一档，说它最快与延迟阶梯完全相反。
竞价 SLA 是硬约束，超时请求会被丢弃，不是「超一点没关系」。
optionExplanations_en: Adding GPUs raises throughput but can't cut the inherent per-generation latency; more machines can't close a magnitude gap.
Correct — 100ms–seconds vs 10ms is an order-of-magnitude gap; under a hard SLA the LLM is out.
An LLM is the slowest tier; calling it fastest contradicts the latency ladder.
The auction SLA is a hard constraint and over-budget requests are dropped — not 'a slight overshoot is fine.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求端到端可用的总时间上限，模型推理只占其中一段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the total end-to-end time allowed per request, of which model inference is only one slice.

q: 补全从经典模型升级到深度学习的三大触发条件：
q_en: Fill in the three triggers to escalate from classical to deep learning.
text: 升级到 DNN 的三大触发：输入是 {{unstructured}}（非结构化）模态需表示学习；标注达 {{millions}}（百万级）DNN 才稳胜 GBDT；需要稠密 embedding 建模复杂 {{interaction}}（交互）如 two-tower 检索。
text_en: Three triggers to escalate to a DNN: {{unstructured}} input modality needing representation learning; {{millions}} of labels where a DNN reliably beats GBDT; dense embeddings for complex {{interaction}} patterns like two-tower retrieval.
why: 记忆钩子：非结构化模态、百万级标注、复杂交互。缺这三者就先留在经典模型，别为「先进」而升级。
why_en: Memory hook: unstructured modality, millions of labels, complex interactions — absent these, stay classical rather than escalate to look advanced.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的形态（表格/文本/图像/音频/视频），决定是否需要表示学习。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modality is the form of data (tabular/text/image/audio/video), deciding whether representation learning is needed.
